JUDGMENT This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 30-04-2022 at about 5.30 p.m., the petitioner was riding the Access 125 Scooter bearing No.KA-41-EQ-8320 on the left side of the road, carefully, cautiously, by observing all the traffic rules, on Tavarekere-Bengaluru main road, VES School opposite Tavarekere town, Bengaluru City.

At that time, all of a sudden the Ashoka Leyland Goods vehicle bearing No.KA-18-C-6478, driven by its driver at high speed,
in rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, without observing any traffic rules, came and dashed against the scooter of the petitioner from behind.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Kenganar Hospital,
Chikkagollarahatti, wherein he took treatment as an in- patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as BESCOM Sub-Contractor and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Tavarekere Police have registered the case against the driver of the said goods vehicle, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.

sentences.text: 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2, in respect of goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-C-6478 and it was valid as on the date of accident.
Further it has sought permission to seek protection under Section 56, 66, 147 and 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provisions under Section 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the goods vehicle bearing No.KA-18-C-6478 was not at all involved in the alleged accident and it has been falsely implicated by the petitioner in collusion with the owner of the vehicle, hospital authorities and the police, in order to get the compensation from the respondent No.1.

The petitioner was himself negligent in causing the accident Further it is contended that, the petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties namely the driver of goods vehicle.
In fact the driver of insured vehicle was necessary party for the adjudication of the above claim.
Further it is contended that, the petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident and thereby he has violated Section 129 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, as on the date of accident, the driver of the goods vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence and the said vehicle was not having valid permit and fitness certificate.
The respondent No.1 knowing fully well that the driver did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle and willfully entrusted his vehicle to the said driver.
Thereby, the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy, hence this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained,
medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

It is admitted that, he is the owner of the Ashok Leyland Goods Vehicle bearing No.KA-18-C-6478 and it was insured with the respondent No.1 insurance company, vide insurance policy No.61023883 and it was valid from 04-10-2021 to 03-10-2022.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the said vehicle was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same, as on the date of accident.
If at all, any compensation is awarded to the petitioner, then the liability has to be saddled on the respondent No.1, who is the insurer of the alleged vehicle.
Further it has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:

On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 8, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-C-6478 and dashing the same to the scooter of the petitioner from behind.
Due to said impact the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.8, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the offending goods vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-18-C-6478.
13.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-C-6478 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

The respondent No.1 and 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and the respondent No.1 has taken specific defence that, the said accident has occurred solely due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the scooter himself and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-C-6478.
But, the respondent No.1 has failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.2, who is the representative/Legal Officer of respondent No.1 insurance company, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of scooter by the petitioner himself and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending goods vehicle.
If really the said accident has taken place due to the negligence of the petitioner himself, the same could have been easily established by examining the eye-witness to the alleged accident.
But, the respondent No.1 has not taken any strain to examine the independent eye-witness to the alleged accident, for the reasons best known to it.

In such circumstances, there is absolutely no independent corroborative evidence on record to show that, at the time of accident the petitioner was riding the motorcycle in rash and negligent manner and the accident has taken place due to his self negligence and the offending Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-C-6478 has been falsely implicated by the petitioner.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-C-6478 and dashing the same to the scooter of the petitioner from behind and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body in the said accident.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the scooter by the petitioner or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summary and Ex.P.16 case sheet, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.

The petitioner has suffered 1) fracture right zygomatic arch, 2) abrasions over right side face, 3) abrasions over right foot, 4) small cut wound right ear, 5) hypokalaemia and 6)

On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-C-6478 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held

Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-C-6478 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained 1) fracture right zygomatic arch, 2) abrasions over right side face, 3) abrasions over right foot, 4) small cut wound right ear, 5) hypokalaemia and 6)
hypertension and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants,
transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
The petitioner has deposed that, earlier to the accident, he was working as BESCOM Sub-Contractor and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
But, the petitioner has neither produced any document nor examined the doctor to establish that, due to injuries sustained in the accident he has suffered any physical disability or deformity.

The petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered any physical disability and he is not in a position to continue his avocation or perform his regular work and thereby, he has lost his earning capacity.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation under head loss of future income due to permanent physical disability does not arise at all.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
ii) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 14 medical bills, as per Ex.P.10.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.2,10,894/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,10,894/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injury i.e. 1)

sentences.text: As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 6 days from 30-04-2022 to 05-05-2022, in Kenganar Hospital, Bengaluru.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 6 days in Kenganar Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent some amount towards attendant charges during the said period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 6 = Rs.6,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 6 days in Kenganar Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent some amount towards food and nourishment during the said period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 6 = Rs.4,800/-
is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Gangenahalli Village, Tavarekere Hobli,
Bengaluru South, the accident has occurred on Tavarekere, Bengaluru main road, opposite VES School, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru South and he has taken treatment at Kenganar Hospital,
Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as BESCOM Sub-Contractor and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do work and continue his avocation.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as BESCOM Sub-Contractor and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2022.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month.
The petitioner has taken treatment for 6 days as in-patient at Kenganar Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injury caused to him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore,
Rs.15,500 x 2 = Rs.31,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 44 years and unfortunately he has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident and undergone treatment for 6 days as in-patient in Kenganar Hospital,
Bengaluru.
Further, he might have taken rest for about two months.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities during the said period would be just and reasonable.

21. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-C- 6478.
As per Ex.R.6 insurance policy bearing No.61023883, issued by the respondent No.1, in respect of offending Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle bearing No.KA-18-C-6478 was valid from 04-10-2021 to 03-10-2022.

Further,

The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.

23. On the other hand, the learned counsel for petitioner vehemently argued that, there is no breach of any fundamental terms and conditions of the policy, as alleged by the respondent No.1.

Further argued that, it is settled principle of law that, even if there is a breach of any fundamental condition of the policy, recognised under Sec.149(2) of Motor vehicles Act, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation to the third party and recover the same from the insured.

24. As rightly argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1, as per the Ex.R.2 B-Register extract and Ex.R.3 permit particulars, the permit issued by the R.T.O., Chikamangalur, in respect of offending Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-C-6478 was valid from 01-09-2023 to 31-08-2028.

Further, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle has not produced any document to show that, prior to 01-09-2023 or more particularly as on the date of accident i.e.
30-04-2022 his vehicle was having valid permit to ply at the place of accident.

But, mere for the reason that, the offending vehicle was not having permit as on the date accident, the respondent No.1 insurance company cannot be exonerated from its liability to indemnify the insured/respondent No.2, unless it is established that, the offending vehicle was not fit or under good condition to be plied on the public road, as on the date of accident and due to unfit condition of the vehicle the accident has taken place.
In the instant case, there are no such specific allegations in respect of offending vehicle and even nothing with respect to same has been stated in the Ex.P.6 Motor Vehicle Accident report.

Further, it is not a defence available to the insurer under Sec.150(2)
of Motor Vehicle Act, to exonerate the respondent No.1 from its liability to indemnify the insured/respondent No.2,

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The respondent No.1 and 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and the respondent No.1 has taken specific defence that, the said accident has occurred solely due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the scooter himself and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-C-6478.
Except the self serving statements of R.W.2, who is the representative/Legal Officer of respondent No.1 insurance company, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of scooter by the petitioner himself and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending goods vehicle.
If really the said accident has taken place due to the negligence of the petitioner himself, the same could have been easily established by examining the eye-witness to the alleged accident.
But, the respondent No.1 has not taken any strain to examine the independent eye-witness to the alleged accident, for the reasons best known to it.
In such circumstances, there is absolutely no independent corroborative evidence on record to show that, at the time of accident the petitioner was riding the motorcycle in rash and negligent manner and the accident has taken place due to his self negligence and the offending Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-C-6478 has been falsely implicated by the petitioner.

5 14.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Reports, which are marked as Ex.P.6, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner/rider of scooter bearing No.KA-41-EQ-8320 , then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-C- 6478.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-C-6478 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.
16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held

6 18.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as BESCOM Sub-Contractor and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Further,
the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA- 18-C-6478 the accident in question has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
22.
Further, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle has not produced any document to show that, prior to 01-09-2023 or more particularly as on the date of accident i.e.
30-04-2022 his vehicle was having valid permit to ply at the place of accident.
But, mere for the reason that, the offending vehicle was not having permit as on the date accident, the respondent No.1 insurance company cannot be exonerated from its liability to indemnify the insured/respondent No.2, unless it is established that, the offending vehicle was not fit or under good condition to be plied on the public road, as on the date of accident and due to unfit condition of the vehicle the accident has taken place.
In the instant case, there are no such specific allegations in respect of offending vehicle and even nothing with respect to same has been stated in the Ex.P.6 Motor Vehicle Accident report.
Further, it is not a defence available to the insurer under Sec.150(2)
of Motor Vehicle Act, to exonerate the respondent No.1 from its liability to indemnify the insured/respondent No.2,
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, mere for the reason that, the respondent No.1 has failed to establish that, his insured vehicle was not having valid permit to ply the said vehicle at the place of accident, as on the date of accident, the insurance company cannot be exonerated from its liability to indemnify the respondent No.2 25.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, there is no breach of any fundamental terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the respondent No.2.
